# java-guardrails 0.3.0

NullAway can now be adopted one package at a time, with measurement and a compiler proof before
the gate is accepted. This release also strengthens source restoration across all falsifiers and
keeps a PMD ratchet from weakening CPD.

- **Optional NullAway adoption.** `measure-nullaway` inventories exact JSpecify package defaults
  and reports compiler findings. Playbook 30 covers package selection, annotations, fixes and
  proof; `assess` and the skill route to it without changing the default gate order. Error Prone
  integration is required; cleanup of other Error Prone findings is independent.
- **Causal compiler proof.** `falsify nullaway --module MODULE --package PACKAGE` first requires
  a valid unannotated probe to compile successfully, then changes only its return value to null.
  Acceptance requires compilation failure and the named NullAway diagnostic. This supports WARN
  enforced by `failOnWarning=true` and rejects unrelated failures as proof. It proves the default
  for the new class, without auditing existing declaration opt-outs, suppressions or exclusions.
- **Reliable reports.** NullAway measurement retains diagnostic columns, separates upstream
  reactor findings, handles ANSI output and refuses successful quiet output that hides diagnostics.
  Inventory ignores marker-like text in comments and string literals.
- **Source restoration for every falsifier.** Plants restore on Ctrl-C and SIGTERM and stop the
  active build. Restoration preserves concurrent edits and replacement files; planting refuses
  symbolic links and collisions with existing files. Signal behavior is tested on Linux;
  SIGKILL, JVM crashes and Windows cleanup remain unproven.
- **PMD allowance isolated from CPD.** Separate Maven executions keep CPD at zero even with a
  positive `pmd.maxAllowedViolations`. `verify` and `pmd:check@pmd-gate` use that PMD ratchet;
  plain `pmd:check` remains strict zero. Direct CPD goals remain strict zero.

## Upgrading

Existing target projects own copies of the Maven slices; updating the skill does not change
their builds. For PMD, copy the revised `maven/pmd.plugin.xml`, add the default
`pmd.maxAllowedViolations` property from `maven/properties.xml`, and convert old positive common
plugin allowances into per-module properties. Remove old plugin-level allowances in parent and
child POMs, then rerun both falsifiers as described in playbook 10. Other existing decisions are
read as before. NullAway is opt-in; follow playbook 30 for each selected package.
